show: verb
let someone see something
typical: show + person + thing, show sth to sb. NOT for: explaining how.
Show me your passport.
She showed us the photos from her trip.
verb
explain how to do something by doing it yourself
typical: show sb how to do sth. NOT for: only displaying an object.
She showed me how to use the machine.
Can you show him how it works?
verb
give information in a picture, map or figures
typical: map/graph/photo/figures + show + noun. NOT for: people explaining.
The map shows the main rivers of the region.
The figures show a rise in prices.
verb
guide someone to a place
typical: show sb to/into/round + place. NOT for: pointing at objects.
Let me show you to your room.
He showed us around the castle.
verb
(of a film or programme) be broadcast or presented
typical: be shown on TV/in cinemas. NOT for: people showing things.
The film is shown on television tonight.
The match was shown live.
verb
be easy to see or notice
typical: it shows (on your face/clothes). NOT for: deliberate display.
Her happiness shows in her face.
The dirt doesn't show on dark clothes.
noun
a television, radio or stage programme
typical: TV/radio/talk show, a show starts at eight. NOT for: exhibition of objects.
We watched a funny show last night.
The show starts at eight.
noun
a public display or exhibition
typical: a fashion/flower/car show, a show of support. NOT for: entertainment programmes.
The art show opens on Friday.
Thousands came to the car show.
start: typical: start + -ing/to + verb, start + noun. NOT for: events starting by themselves.
(of an event or activity) begin to happen
typical: film/lesson/meeting/season starts. NOT for: people beginning an action.
create or establish a business or organization
typical: start a business/company/club. NOT for: engines.
She started a small business last year.
begin a new job or school
typical: start work/school/college/a job. NOT for: events.
I start my new job on Monday.
The children start school in September.
make an engine or machine begin to work, or begin to work
typical: start the car/engine, the car won't start. NOT for: events.
typical: start out/off, start for + place. NOT for: beginning an activity.
We'll start early to avoid traffic.
deliberately cause something, often something bad
typical: start a fire/fight/argument/rumour. NOT for: neutral beginnings.
Someone started a rumour about her.
(of prices or amounts) have a lowest value
typical: start at/from + amount. NOT for: events.
